rows.en: Recognized by the Vajra through Ranka, Sheryl
was at last freed from the grip of the V-type virus.
Sheryl and Ranka sang, each striving to outdo the other.
rows.notes: Source is present tense; narration put in past tense per brief.

rows.en: Their song gave strength to a renewed counterattack against Grace.
What's more, the power of Ranka and Sheryl's songs
even freed the Vajra that Grace had held under her control.
The Vajra and humanity formed a united front and stood against Grace.
Faced with that power, Grace was no longer any match for them.
Grace's ambition to rule the galaxy by exploiting both the Vajra and humanity
was thus shattered.
Their battle over, the Frontier fleet set down on the Vajra homeworld.
rows.notes: Home planet rendered with glossary term 'Vajra homeworld'.

rows.en: Humanity and the Vajra: utterly different life-forms that never got along.
rows.notes: Source is a verbless noun-phrase sentence (utterly different ecologies, never compatible); kept as a fragment in narration style. | review: Tense/meaning: source is past ('had never been compatible'); timeless 'never able to coexist' contradicts row 174, where they coexist. | review: refit: 'had never been able to get along' -> 'never got along'

rows.en: And yet it turned out they could understand one another.
And so a new world was born, where the Vajra and humanity live side by side...
Revived after absorbing Sara, the Bird Human used its overwhelming might
rows.notes: review: rebalance: takes 'overwhelming might' from row 176

rows.en: to wreak utter destruction, bent on wiping out a humanity that kept fighting.
rows.notes: review: rebalance/refit: restructured after moving the might clause to row 175

rows.en: In that hopeless situation, Shin's voice managed to awaken Sara's heart.
But Operation Iconoclasm had already been set in motion.
Reaction weapons flew to destroy the Bird Human, deemed uncontrollable.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'now judged to be beyond control' -> 'out-of-control' (the 'judged' nuance is lost) | review: keep "deemed uncontrollable"

rows.en: To protect Earth, Mayan Island, and above all Shin, Sara flew off into space,
rows.notes: Sara is the subject of row 180 in the source; kept her name in this row. | review: rebalance: takes 'flew off into space' from row 181

rows.en: taking with her the reaction weapons she had sealed away with her own power.
rows.notes: review: rebalance: 'flew off into space' moved to row 180

rows.en: Thus both ruin by the Bird Human and reaction-weapon fallout were averted.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'annihilation' -> 'ruin'; 'contamination by the reaction weapons' -> 'reaction-weapon fallout'

rows.en: But Shin's fighter had lost all control and was simply plummeting.
His ejection system had failed too, leaving him no way to escape.
rows.notes: Shin is male per glossary.

rows.en: Shin's fighter, which seemed certain to crash,
began to climb, wrapped in a mysterious light,
rows.notes: review: rebalance: period -> comma so row 187 continues the sentence (one sentence in the source)

rows.en: watched by %s, %s and the islanders,
rows.notes: Rows 187-188 are an inverted trailing clause after the sentence ending in 186; restored the verb 'It rose' so the row reads as a sentence. Placeholders kept gender-neutral. | review: refit: 'It rose as ... looked on' -> 'watched by'; 'the people of Mayan Island' -> 'the islanders' (Mayan Island named in row 180)

rows.en: as if chasing after Sara, who had vanished into space...
Before the enemy's overwhelming strength, the Macross seemed helpless.
But then, an unexpected ally appeared.
Moved by Minmay's song, Vrlitwhai and a faction of the Zentradi forces
had risen in revolt against Boddole Zer.
rows.notes: Short form of Golg Boddole Zer, as the source uses the short form.

rows.en: Refusing to let humanity be wiped out and its culture lost,
Vrlitwhai's forces covered the Macross as it drove on through space.
Along the way, it cut down Zentradi soldiers left bewildered by Minmay's song.
rows.notes: Source is a trailing fragment after 194; restored subject and verb.

rows.en: At last, the Macross closed in on the heart of the Main Fleet,
rows.notes: Verb 'closed in' placed in 196 for English word order; 197 keeps the fortress name, matching the source cut.

rows.en: Boddole Zer's mobile fortress.
The only way for humanity to survive was to destroy the enemy's nerve center.
As the Macross launched its attack,
the Valkyries stormed into the mobile fortress.
The Main Fleet's commander and core unit of Boddole Zer's mobile fortress,
rows.notes: review: refit: possessive; second 'the' dropped

rows.en: Golg Boddole Zer, was destroyed.
With its chain of command gone, the Main Fleet
no longer had the strength to attack the Macross.
And so the Space War, fierce beyond measure, came to an end.
rows.notes: Source says 'the interstellar war' with no ordinal; rendered 'the Space War' (glossary only has 'Space War I').

rows.en: Leaving behind the legend of Minmay's song...
rows.notes: Literally 'together with the legend of Minmay's song'.

rows.en: The Galaxy Whale was struck by the poachers' reaction weapon.
But the whale shrugged off the reaction weapon as if it were nothing.
Seeing this, Basara began singing to the whale.
And then something unexpected happened.
The Galaxy Whale responded to Basara's song and let out a cry.
Or rather, it began singing along with Basara's song.
Singing together with Basara, the Galaxy Whale
absorbed tremendous energy and shook the ground of Zola.
It held a power that overwhelmed all who witnessed it.
Eventually the whales vanished into the far reaches of the galaxy, still singing.
And so the session that seemed like it might never end
between Basara and the whales came to a close.
rows.notes: Source noun for whale is unmarked for number; used plural to match row 216.

rows.en: Thanks to the efforts of the Zolan Star Patrol, the poachers were swept away.
rows.notes: Source just says 'the patrol unit'; mapped to glossary 'Zolan Star Patrol' (its ja form is marked unconfirmed).

rows.en: Satisfied after singing his heart out with the whales, Basara
left Zola behind and flew off to the far reaches of space.
Ahead of %s and %s, who had also left Zola,
rows.notes: review: refit: leading 'And' dropped

rows.en: lay a certain space fleet bound for the center of the galaxy...
Annihilate the enemy of the U.N. Forces:\nthe Anti-U.N. Forces.
Commencing the operation to wipe out the U.N.'s foe: the "Anti-U.N. Forces."\nAnnihilate the Anti-U.N. TYPE-29 fighter formation.
rows.notes: Source sets the organization name in brackets; kept as quotation marks. | review: refit: "U.N. Forces" to "U.N.'s", "enemy" to "foe"; L2 drops repeated "Forces'"

rows.en: Annihilate the enemy of the U.N. Forces:\nthe Anti-U.N. Forces.
rows.notes: Same text as row 224.

rows.en: Commencing the operation to wipe out the U.N.'s foe: the "Anti-U.N. Forces."\nAnnihilate the Anti-U.N. TYPE-29 fighter formation.
rows.notes: Same text as row 225. | review: refit: "U.N. Forces" to "U.N.'s", "enemy" to "foe"; L2 drops repeated "Forces'"

rows.en: As part of conversion training for the VF-0,\nengage in a mock battle.
The "VF-0": a variable fighter developed with the ASS-1's OverTechnology.\nTo survive the battles ahead, you'll now undergo VF-0 conversion training.
rows.notes: ASS-1 is not a glossary entry (only mentioned in notes); bare 'VF-0' not an entry either (only VF-0S/D/A). Kept as written. | review: term added to glossary | review: refit: tighter wording

rows.en: Annihilate the Anti-U.N. Forces'\nnew variable fighter unit.
The Anti-U.N. Forces made a surprise attack with VFs built using our tech.\nSortie at once and annihilate the Anti-U.N. variable fighters.
rows.notes: review: refit: "variable fighters" abbreviated to "VFs" in L1, "technology" to "tech"; second Anti-U.N. mention shortened

rows.en: As part of your training,\nfight a mock battle against Major Focker.
rows.notes: Source rank is shosa = Major; glossary lists Roy as Lieutenant in the Zero era, but this briefing says Major, so the source is followed.

rows.en: To prepare for the escalating Anti-U.N. war, we'll hold a mock battle drill.\nWin the mock battle against U.N. Forces ace Major Roy Focker.
rows.notes: Same rank issue as row 232. | review: refit: "mock battle as training" to "mock battle drill"; L2 aligned with row 265 (same source line)

rows.en: To stop the theft of the AFOS fragment,\nannihilate the Anti-U.N. Forces.
rows.notes: review: refit: 'from being seized' -> 'the theft of'

rows.en: The Anti-U.N. Forces are trying to seize the AFOS fragment on Mayan Island.\nExpect unfamiliar underwater combat, but wipe out the Anti-U.N. at all costs.
rows.notes: review: refit: tighter wording, second mention "Anti-U.N."

rows.en: To defend the AFOS fragment,\nannihilate the Anti-U.N. Forces.
The Anti-U.N. Forces attack the Asuka to seize the AFOS fragment under study.\nDefend the carrier Asuka and annihilate the Anti-U.N. at all costs.
rows.notes: review: refit: restructured so the Asuka is named as the target in L1; second mention "Anti-U.N."

rows.en: To defend the AFOS fragment,\nannihilate the Anti-U.N. Forces.
rows.notes: Same text as row 236.

rows.en: The Anti-U.N. Forces attack the Asuka to seize the AFOS fragment under study.\nDefend the carrier Asuka and annihilate the Anti-U.N. at all costs.
rows.notes: Same text as row 237. | review: refit: restructured so the Asuka is named as the target in L1; second mention "Anti-U.N."

rows.en: Find the Bird Human's head and\nretrieve it to the target area.

uncertain: row 172: verbless source sentence kept as a narration fragment
row 187: restored verb 'It rose' for the inverted trailing clause in rows 187-188
rows 196-197, 201-202: sentence cuts adjusted for English word order (verb in 196; apposition across 201-202)
row 205: 'the Space War' for the interstellar war (no ordinal in source)
row 219: patrol unit mapped to 'Zolan Star Patrol' (glossary ja form unconfirmed)
rows 232-233: Roy Focker's rank given as Major per source; glossary says Lieutenant for the Zero era
missing_glossary: ASS-1 (the alien ship, row 229): used as 'ASS-1'; only mentioned in glossary notes
VF-0 (bare model name, rows 228-229): glossary only has VF-0S/D/A Phoenix; used 'VF-0'
